title: Protocol to image and quantify nuclear pore complexes using high-resolution laser scanning confocal microscopy
protocol: Remove fibronectin from each well using a p1000 pipette or aspiration system.
Plate an appropriate number of cells per coverslip to achieve 80–90% confluency at time of fixation.
Add approximately 400–500 μL of culture media to each well.
Place the plate in a 37°C 5% CO2 incubator and incubate for 16–24 hours.
The following morning, remove media from each well.
Add approximately 500 μL of sterile 1× PBS to each well.
Gently rinse the cells by running PBS over the coverslip to remove any dead or unattached cells.
Remove PBS from each well.
Add 500 μL of culture media to each well.
Continue to incubate cells until ready for fixation.
Remove culture media from cells.
Wash cells with 1× PBS.
Fix cells in ∼500 μL 4% paraformaldehyde for 20 min at 20–25°C.
Wash cells 3 times with 1× PBS.
Permeabilize cells with ∼500 μL of 0.5% Triton-X 100 to completely cover the cells.
Incubate for 10 min at 20–25°C.
Wash cells one time with 1× PBS.
Block cells by adding ∼500 μL blocking buffer.
Incubate for 2 h at 20–25°C.
Dilute primary antibody in blocking buffer as per the manufacturer's recommendation.
Calculate at least 400–500 μL of diluted antibody solution per well.
If using multiple primary antibodies, dilute all in the same buffer to their intended concentrations.
Store diluted antibody mixture at 4°C until ready for use.
After 2 hours, remove blocking buffer and add diluted primary antibody mixture to each well.
Incubate with primary antibody mixture at 4°C for 16–24 hours.
Alternatively, add approximately 100 μL of diluted antibody to the coverslip and cover with parafilm to prevent evaporation.
The following morning, remove the primary antibody solution from the wells.
Wash cells in 1× PBS and rock for 5 minutes at 20–25°C.
Repeat washing step three times in total.
While cells are being washed, dilute secondary antibody in 1× PBS according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute all antibodies in 1× PBS buffer.
Remove third PBS wash and add 400–500 μL of secondary antibody solution to each well.
Incubate the cells at 20–25°C in the dark for 2 h.
Add ∼ 100 μL of diluted antibody to the coverslip.
Cover with a small piece of parafilm to prevent evaporation and drying.
Store the plate in complete darkness, either in a drawer or covered with aluminum foil.
Remove secondary antibody after 2 h.
Wash cells 3 times in 1× PBS for 5 min.
Dilute Hoechst in 1× PBS at approximately 1:500–1:1000 or optimize according to manufacturer’s recommendation.
Incubate at 20–25°C in the dark for 5 min.
Wash briefly in 1× PBS.
Carefully remove coverslip from the well using fine-tipped forceps, taking care not to flip the coverslip or scratch cells from surface of the coverslip.
Clean microscope slide with Kimwipe and 100% ethanol.
Cut two thin strips of parafilm (approx. 2 mm × 15 mm).
Place the parafilm strips on the microscope slide.
Add one drop of mounting media to the middle of the round coverslip containing fixed cells.
Cover the cells with a 22 mm × 22 mm glass coverslip #1.5.
Seal all four edges of the square coverslip with nail polish.
Seal the edges of the glass coverslip with fingernail polish.
Allow to dry before imaging.
Mount cardiomyocytes on round Thermanox coverslips for optimal attachment.
Use cover glass for mounting without distorting the light path.
Apply spacers to prevent compression of nuclei by capillary forces.
Use an oil-immersion lens for highest possible resolution.
Place slide containing mounted cells onto the stage of the confocal microscope.
Ensure the glass coverslip faces toward the objective.
Locate cell nuclei using the DAPI channel under the 10× or 20× objective lens.
Switch to the Plan Apo Lambda 100× oil immersion objective lens.
Add 1 drop of Immersion Oil Type B to the surface of the lens.
Identify cells with a smooth nuclear border by bringing the edge of the nucleus into focus.
Select only cells in interphase where the entire nuclear envelope can be seen as a disc.
Set the pinhole size to 0.7AU for selected cells.
Set scanning format size to 1024 × 1024 pixels with a pixel dwell time of 1.1 μsec.
Press the SCAN button to begin scanning.
Adjust laser power and gain at the optimal focal plane for each subcellular structure (nucleus, nuclear pores, etc).
Modify focus as needed to avoid oversaturation.
Evaluate Look Up Table (LUT) histogram for appropriate display of low through high range of intensity.
Take an image of the cell of interest by selecting CAPTURE.
Save both the ND file and the captured raw data containing separate channel images for each fluorophore.
Save a TIFF file representing all fluorophores.
Select SCAN again to image the nucleus.
Crop the image so the nucleus engulfs the entire scanning field while leaving room to visualize the entire nuclear envelope and surrounding nuclear pores.
Set the scanning format size to 2048 × 2048 pixels.
Set the pixel dwell time to 3.2 μsec.
Decrease the pinhole size to 0.4AU.
Re-adjust the laser power and gain as needed for each laser.
Obtain a 3D image using the Z-series Acquisition on Nikon Elements software.
Select the Acquisition tab and click the Z-stack box.
Set the Z range by setting the top and bottom positions of the nucleus.
Focus on the top of the nucleus and press the Top button.
Move the focus to the bottom of the nucleus and press the Bottom button.
Convert 3D Z-stack ND file to a maximum intensity projection image.
Define binary threshold using Fiji (ImageJ).
Right click in the Max Intensity Projection image and select New Document.
Obtain binary threshold under the DAPI channel by clicking within the nucleus in several areas.
Define parameters in thresholding dialogue box to determine binary.
Convert Binary to ROI.
Select the ROI tab located on the toolbar above the image.
Select Move Binary to ROI.
Right click within the ROI and select Copy ROI.
Paste ROI into the ORIGINAL Z-Stack image.
Select proper Z-stack optical sections for quantification.
Choose the top and bottom sections of the nucleus showing pores on the surface and along the edge of the nuclear envelope (NE).
Adjust parameters in the spot detection dialogue box iteratively.
Hit OK once the parameters are defined for optimal object inclusion and exclusion.
Open Automated Measurement Result under the Analysis tab in the toolbar.
Select ROI DATA from the first drop down box.
Use Gaussian Blur on photomicrograph of nuclear pores stained with Mab414 with sigma radius of 1 and 2.
Subtract the photomicrograph with sigma 2 from that with sigma 1 (Difference of Gaussians).
Threshold and binarize the image of nuclear pore complexes.
Digitally quantify to yield the number of nuclear pores.
Load raw data file into ImageJ.
Create duplicates of the original file for the nuclear pore detection channel and name them as 1 and 2.
Threshold on the DAPI channel to create an ROI of the nucleus.
Edit selection -> Create Selection.
Copy ROI to both duplicates.
Apply Gaussian Blur to each duplicate image.
Process -> Filter -> Gaussian Blur, use Sigma (radius) of 2 for Image 2 and Sigma (radius) of 1 for Image 1.
Find Difference of Gaussians (DoG) by subtracting image 2 from image 1.
Process -> Image Calculator. Choose “1” as image 1 and “2” as image 2, operation = subtract; create new window.
Adjust brightness and contrast.
Threshold the nuclear pores on the DoG image.
Separate particles: Process -> Binary -> Watershed.
Remove errant particles if necessary: Process -> Binary -> Open.
Set measurement parameters in the analysis software.
Check the Limit Threshold box.
Check the Bounding rectangle box to count particles within the region of interest (ROI) only.
Threshold on the DAPI channel to create an ROI of the nucleus.
Apply binary open operation.
Create a selection for the ROI.
Copy the ROI.
Adjust brightness and contrast.
Threshold the nuclear pores.
Separate particles using watershed segmentation.
Set size measurement parameters.
Analyze particles.
Set size parameters and additional outputs needed.
Hit OK to obtain summary measurements.
